Hi Neha,

Thanks — wed love a walkthrough of Redwood next week. We have small teams in the US (NY), UK (London) and APAC (Singapore). I can do:

- Thu 20 May, 15:00-15:30 (local time for one of our UK folks)

Hi Evan — thanks for the agenda. Quick note: when you suggested Wed 19 May 10:00 I see that my calendar invite landed at 07:00 PT for a teammate, and at 15:00 for someone in the UK — the usual UTC offsets mean the "10:00 ET" label can get interpreted differently if a participant's calendar defaults to local zone.

To avoid a silent shift: would you/your team be ok with either of these two canonical UTC slots so we can send invites that lock across zones?

- Option A: 2026-05-19 14:00 UTC (which would be 10:00 ET / 15:00 BST / 22:00 SGT)
- Option B: 2026-05-20 08:00 UTC (04:00 ET / 09:00 BST / 16:00 SGT)

I know Option B is brutal for US folk; Option A hits the UK comfortably but pushes APAC late — if Tom is available after hours, Option A is our preference for a single 30-minute demo.

Karthik and Grace are ccd in case we want to propose a different fallback (e.g., two short regional demos). Ill attach our product deck (v2) so Tom has context in case the time ends up late.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: redwood-deck-v2.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)

Heads up — I pulled the initial calendar invite Neha referenced. It looks like whoever created it used their calendar default (PDT) which is why some internal folks saw a 07:00 start. Thats an easy trap when invites are created in a different local zone and recipients rely on the raw hour rather than a canonical UTC stamp.

Two quick operational asks so we dont have to play follow-the-invite:

1) Can we pick a UTC time in the body of the invite and explicitly set the event time in UTC when we create the Google Calendar event? That way the invite is consistent no matter what client you use.
2) If Option A (2026-05-19 14:00 UTC) is acceptable, we should offer Tom the option of joining for the first 20 minutes only and send a recording for anything after. If thats not acceptable, we spin up a short APAC-friendly slot the following day.

Neha, if Evan confirms Option A I can create the invite in UTC and include a short note: "Event time shown in UTC; local conversions are listed below."

- Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering
